title: Role-play lab: six client conversations
objectives: Practise six realistic client conversations in pairs.
Score yourself against what a good response includes.
Link each scenario to a L.E.A.R.N. stage.
body_md:
Run in pairs: one plays the client, one the distributor. The trainer scores on the points listed.

| # | Scenario | Stage tested | What a good response includes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | A 26-year-old with a new job wants to "put ₹2 lakh in the fund that gave the highest return last year". | E, A | Checks emergency fund and insurance; asks goals and horizon; explains recency bias; suggests SIP or STP into a suitable category. |
| 2 | A client asks, "Why should I invest through you when direct plans are cheaper?" | L | Acknowledges the cost difference honestly; explains selection, reviews, servicing and behavioural support; never dismisses direct plans. |
| 3 | A client invested 1 year ago and says, "My fund hasn't grown. Was it the wrong time?" | R, N | Shows XIRR vs benchmark and category; explains that 1 year is too short for equity; reconnects to goal; no promise of recovery. |
| 4 | Markets have fallen 15%. A retired client wants to redeem everything. | N | Calm, goal-based response; checks whether near-term money is in debt; separates emergency need from panic; records the conversation. |
| 5 | A client has 11 funds from different apps and friends. | R | Pulls the CAS; checks overlap; proposes consolidation with tax and exit load in mind. |
| 6 | A widow calls; her husband's folios have no nominee. | Niche | Empathy first; explains transmission process and documents; offers to coordinate with the RTA; reviews nominations for her own folios. |
example: Run scenario 1 in pairs: one plays a 26-year-old who wants ₹2 lakh in last year's top fund. The distributor checks the emergency fund and insurance, asks the goal and horizon, and explains recency bias.
say: Let's understand what this money is for first.
Let me show you the fund's five-year record, including the bad years.
never: Let's just do what you asked.
I'll tell you what you want to hear.

check.q: A client has ₹20 lakh for a 10-year goal but fears investing at the wrong time. Best method?
o: STP from a liquid/debt fund into equity over 6–12 months
Invest all of it in small-cap today
Keep it in a savings account until markets fall
check.why: STP stages a large sum into equity and reduces timing regret.

check.q: Markets fall 15%. What is the first thing you do?
o: Wait for clients to call you
Advise all clients to pause SIPs
Proactively call clients, starting with recent and first-time investors
Move all equity holdings to debt
check.why: Call first, before clients call in panic, and reconnect them to their goals.

check.q: A client switches from Fund A to Fund B in the same fund house. Can it be taxable?
o: Yes, because a switch is a redemption plus a purchase
No, switches within one fund house are tax-free
Only if the amount exceeds ₹1 lakh
Only exit load applies, never tax
check.why: Check tax and exit load before every switch, even within the same fund house.
